title: task list --across-refs caches per ref by .quest tree hash so an unchanged ref is never re-read (ODOC-610 / DEC-282 (a1) item 5)
description:
CARRIER from ODOC-610 / DEC-282 item 5, RE-SCOPED to a build by DEC-282 (a1) on 2026-11-19. Read BY REF from opum-doc origin/dev 68734a01 (.quest/planning.json, decision DEC-282, outcomes and (a1)).

Original filing, 2026-11-18, verbatim: "quest-cli: profile task list --across-refs at about 2000 tasks and report before changing anything. Lower priority." The measurement was then the deliverable.

(a1) moved item 5 from "profile first" to build, verbatim: "5. (revised) `task list --across-refs` caches its result per ref, keyed by each ref's .quest tree hash, so an unchanged ref is never re-read. A repeat call with no ref changed answers from the cache, quickly. Proof: wall time and process count at about 2,000 tasks and 40 refs, before and after, plus a test that a second call with unchanged refs reads nothing."

The live case behind it, verbatim from (a1): "A live case on mbam5 at 02:24Z: the Mac's load was 41, with 4-9 concurrent `quest task list --across-refs --allow-partial --json` processes each running 60-90 s ... The repository has 2,313 tasks and 47 worktrees of one clone."

Ships with DEC-282 items 1-4, 7 and 8 in the next lore/quest pair release.

acceptanceCriteria.text: task list --across-refs caches its result per ref, keyed by each ref's .quest tree hash, so an unchanged ref is never re-read
A repeat call with no ref changed answers from the cache without reading any ref
Wall time and process count are measured at about 2,000 tasks and 40 refs, before and after the change, and recorded on this task
A test shows that a second call with unchanged refs reads nothing
bun run check exits 0 with the new test included

implementationNotes: RE-SCOPED 2026-11-19 by DEC-282 (a1), read by ref at opum-doc origin/dev 68734a01: item 5 moved from 'profile first' to build. The old AC1 (profile at about 2000 tasks and report before changing anything) and AC2 (no change before that report) are superseded by the build ACs now on the record; the old scope measured, this one caches per ref keyed by the .quest tree hash and proves it with before/after wall time and process counts plus a no-read second call. Original filing text is kept in the description rather than rewritten.

#763 round 1: REQUEST_CHANGES at c342583873ccf575a982e403a92ea047edf502f8 from the Opus unit quest-cli-review-763, model claude-opus-5-5 (verified by the leader), review worktree review-563-c342583. Leader round-2 scope (one pass): F1 record cold and warm wall time and process count before and after at about 2,000 tasks and 40 refs with the population, fixture counts and cache dir size; F2 prune to the newest 64 by mtime, touch on hit, unlink the temp file on a failed write; F3 remove the unwired whole-result functions and their two tests (they return with QCLI-568 wiring with sha and a request fingerprint in the key); F4 cache the raw location/path/text material keyed by tree hash and re-run the filter, parse, taskState and duplicate check on every read (fingerprint-of-bytes minimum only if the preferred fix costs more than about an hour); F5-F9 all; F10 only if warm wall time at 40 refs is over 5 s. Round 2 is in progress on the same branch. Verdict, byte-verbatim between the relay markers:

VERDICT: REQUEST_CHANGES at c342583873ccf575a982e403a92ea047edf502f8

Reviewer: read-only. I read the PR diff, `across-refs.ts`, `across-refs-cache.ts`, `local-git.ts`, `ports/git.ts`, the new test file and `.quest/tasks/QCLI-563.json`, all at the head SHA above. I had no shell, so none of the numbers below were measured by me. The process and wall-time figures are your claims or my reading of the code, and I label which.

Overall: the per-ref cache keyed by the `.quest` tree hash is sound, and an unreadable ref is never cached, which is correct. Two things block: the measurement is not on the task record, and the cache can grow without limit.

F1 BLOCKING. AC3 is unmet at this head (`.quest/tasks/QCLI-563.json`)
- The record is still `To Do`. Its only implementation note is the 2026-11-19 re-scope, and no before/after measurement is recorded.
- Your claims also have a gap. You give the cold wall time (86.8 s vs 88.7 s) and the warm process count (2,204 → 125), but not the warm wall time. The ruling's "answers from the cache, quickly" is exactly that number.
- Fix: on this branch, record cold and warm wall time and process count, before and after, at about 2,000 tasks and 40 refs. Name the population used (`--ref` ×40 or open-prs) and the tasks/refs count of the fixture. Also record the size of `across-refs-cache/` after the warm run (F2 needs it).

F2 BLOCKING. The cache has no bound and nothing prunes it (`across-refs-cache.ts:178-191`, `writeJsonAtomically`; `AcrossRefsCache.write` at :239)
- Each distinct `.quest` tree hash ever seen gets a full JSON copy of that ref's whole parsed record set. In the live clone that is about 2,300 records per entry, I estimate several MB each (unmeasured).
- `.quest` changes on nearly every tracker commit on `dev` and on most PR heads, so a new entry lands with almost every tracker change seen by any of the clone's worktrees.
- Nothing deletes entries, `git gc` never touches the directory, and it is invisible to users.
- Fix (cheap): on write, prune to the newest K entries by mtime (for example 64), or by age, and touch an entry on a cache hit so mtime means last used.
- Fix (optional, larger): a two-level content-addressed layout. Store tree hash → `[(path, blobOid)]` manifests plus per-blob records, so consecutive `dev` trees share almost all their storage.
- In the same function: if `writeFile` fails part-way (ENOSPC, for example), the temp file is never unlinked. Add `await unlink(temporary).catch(() => {})` in the catch.

F3 SHOULD. The exported whole-result cache can serve a stale sha, and nothing calls it yet (`across-refs-cache.ts:261-344`, `readAcrossRefsCache`/`writeAcrossRefsCache`)
- Its key is ref NAME → per-ref key (the `.quest` tree hash) only.
- The cached result embeds `refProvenance.sha`, `coverage.refsRead[].sha`, `pullRequest` labels and `discoveredAt`.
- So a PR head that moves without touching `.quest` (most commits) would be served the OLD sha in provenance. The docblock caveat names filter and `--allow-partial` but not this.
- Read validation is also shallow: it does not re-validate the entries.
- Nothing in this PR calls these functions, so this is a trap for QCLI-568, not a live bug.
- Fix: remove both functions and their two tests from this PR so they land with QCLI-568's lock. Or, if they stay, fold the planned sha per ref plus a request fingerprint (filter, `--allow-partial`, population) into the key now. Also update the module docblock's "TWO layers" description, since only layer 1 is wired.

F4 SHOULD. A cache written by one quest build is served to another (`across-refs-cache.ts:101` `CACHE_VERSION`, `:229`)
- The cache lives in the common dir, so every worktree's quest build shares it. In this fleet the installed PATH binary and `bun src/cli/main.ts` run side by side in one clone.
- `taskSchema` is a plain `z.object` (`tasks.ts:394`), which STRIPS unknown keys. So build A writes records already reduced to A's schema.
- Re-running `taskState` on read catches a newer build that is stricter. It does not catch a field that A stripped and B reads or filters on. It also does not catch a change to `CONTINUITY_TASK_LOCATIONS` or to the dot-file filter.
- The only guard is a hand-bumped `CACHE_VERSION`.
- Fix (preferred): cache the RAW material instead of parsed `TaskState`, as `{location: [{path, text}]}` keyed by tree hash. Re-run the dot-file filter, `JSON.parse`, `taskState` and the duplicate-id check on every read, and treat a location missing from the entry as a miss. Parsing is cheap next to the process spawns. After that, `CACHE_VERSION` only describes the document shape.
- Fix (minimum): put a build fingerprint in the directory name. The package version alone is not enough, because one version string can name two byte-sets here.

F5 SHOULD. The "never writes" claims are now false
- `across-refs.ts:46` says "THE VIEW NEVER WRITES".
- `main.ts:493` says "Nothing was written -- the view is read-only".
- On that drift path, every ref that DID read has already been written to the cache.
- Fix: scope the promise to refs, tracker records and the working tree, and name the cache under `<git-common-dir>/quest/across-refs-cache/`. Check that the help text at `command-help.ts:190` ("read-only view") still reads true; I would add one clause naming the cache.

F6 SHOULD. Round-trip fidelity is untested on realistic records (`test/qcli563-across-refs-cache.test.ts`, fixture `taskRecord` at about :88)
- Fixture records have no `createdAt`, no gates or `gateEvents`, and empty checklists.
- A cached record goes through `taskState` twice: once on write and again on read (`normalizeCheckList`, gate replay).
- `identity` (task/collision/unresolved) depends on `createdAt`, which the fixtures never set.
- Fix: add one record with `createdAt`, a gate plus its `gateEvents`, and non-empty acceptance criteria. Assert that warm-call entries deep-equal cold-call entries, including `identity`.

F7 NIT. The "changed ref" test does not assert the new content (test, "a changed ref re-reads ONLY that ref")
- It proves the moved `dev` was re-read but not that the answer reflects the edit.
- Fix: assert that T-1's title is "edited on dev".

F8 NIT. The tests depend on order
- That same test commits onto the shared fixture's `dev`.
- The earlier test's premise `dev:.quest == copy:.quest` holds only because it runs first. `fixture.devSha` is stale afterwards.
- Fix: give the mutating test its own branch or fixture.

F9 NIT. No test covers corruption that parses as valid JSON
- The corrupt-entry test writes non-JSON, so the `taskState` re-validation at `across-refs-cache.ts:229` is not exercised.
- Fix: add a well-formed document whose record fails `taskState`, and assert it falls back to a fresh read.

F10 ADVISORY (d). Where the ~125 warm processes likely go (my reading of the code, not measured)
- About three per ref: `resolveLocal` (`rev-parse`) in planning, `hasRevision` (`cat-file -e`), and `treeHash` (`rev-parse <sha>:.quest`).
- Plus a few fixed calls: origin, `commonDirectory`, and `ls-remote`/`gh` for open-prs.
- Cheap win: one `git cat-file --batch-check` fed `<sha>^{commit}` and `<sha>:.quest` lines for every planned ref answers presence and tree oid in one process. Explicit refs can likewise resolve in one multi-arg `rev-parse`. That takes a warm call to under 10 processes.
- Not blocking unless the warm wall time from F1 says "quickly" is unmet.

Checked and sound
- (a) per-ref key:
  - Records are read only under `.quest/<location>`, so the `.quest` tree hash covers them.
  - Ref name, PR label and sha are re-supplied from the plan on every call.
  - Filters, `--include-archived` and lifecycle policy are applied in `buildEntries` after the cache, so they need no key.
  - `--allow-partial` changes only planning.
  - The `root-<tree>` fallback is content-addressed and correct.
  - The only stale paths are F3 (unwired) and F4.
- (b) concurrency: writes go to a unique temp file and `rename` into place in the same directory, so a reader never sees a torn file. Concurrent writers of one key write equivalent content, and the last one wins harmlessly (the exception is F4's mixed builds). Location `<git-common-dir>/quest/across-refs-cache/` is right. Nothing that lists `<common>/quest/` would trip on the new subdirectory: `id-allocation.ts:637` lists the worktree's `.quest`, not the common dir. Bound: none, see F2.
- (c) the no-read test proves it through a seam that counts `listFilesRequired` and `readBlob` on a FRESH service, so the answer must come from disk. Mutants that turn it red: make `AcrossRefsCache.read` return null, or delete `await cache.write(...)` at `across-refs.ts:779`. A key by sha or by ref name is caught by the "two shas, one read" and "changed ref" tests.
- (e) failure modes: every read and write swallows its own errors. `resolveCache` falls back to null, which disables caching without failing. `acrossRefsRefKey` falls back to undefined, which means read without caching. A corrupt entry is a miss. Unreadable refs bypass the write.
- (f) envelope and exit codes: `main.ts` is untouched by the diff, the envelope shape is the same, and `discoveredAt` is stamped fresh on every call. The writer's "envelope unchanged" claim holds by reading the code.

ACs
- AC1 (per-ref cache keyed by the `.quest` tree hash): MET, subject to F2 and F4.
- AC2 (repeat call answers from the cache without reading any ref): MET as "reads no record". `hasRevision` and `treeHash` still run once per ref. That is unavoidable for a content-addressed key, but the record should say "no record read" rather than "nothing read".
- AC3 (wall time and process count before and after, on the task): NOT MET, see F1.
- AC4 (a test shows a second call reads nothing): MET, scored as "reads no record". The test is mutant-sensitive per (c).
- AC5 (`bun run check` exits 0): NOT VERIFIED by me (no shell). It is plausible, since the only other GitPort stand-ins in tests are `as unknown as GitPort` casts that the two new port methods do not break. Cite the CI `source-gates` run on this head.
